options: total number of deaths in a year
rate at which the number of people in a country increases or decreases over time
amount spent by government on health care
number of people who are literate in a country
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: rate at which the number of people in a country increases or decreases over time

Population and Labour Market.text: Rural-urban migration refers to the movement of people from ______.
options: one country to another for trade
villages and rural areas to towns and cities in search of better opportunities
one continent to another for tourism
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: villages and rural areas to towns and cities in search of better opportunities

Population and Labour Market.text: Which of the following is a major cause of rural-urban migration in West Africa?
options: Abundance of fertile farmland in cities
Higher cost of living in rural areas than in cities
Better job opportunities and social amenities in urban areas
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: Better job opportunities and social amenities in urban areas

Population and Labour Market.text: One negative effect of rural-urban migration on rural areas is ______.
options: a shortage of youthful labour for farming
an increase in agricultural labour supply
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: a shortage of youthful labour for farming

Population and Labour Market.text: One negative effect of rural-urban migration on urban areas is ______.
options: reduced pressure on housing and social amenities
overcrowding and pressure on infrastructure and social amenities
an increase in rural agricultural output
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: overcrowding and pressure on infrastructure and social amenities

Population and Labour Market.text: The Malthusian theory of population states that ______.
options: population grows arithmetically while food supply grows geometrically
population and food supply always grow at the same rate
population grows geometrically while food supply grows arithmetically
food supply always exceeds population growth indefinitely
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: population grows geometrically while food supply grows arithmetically

Population and Labour Market.text: According to Malthus, which of the following would serve as a check on population growth?
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: Famine, disease, and war

Population and Labour Market.text: A major criticism of the Malthusian theory of population is that it failed to anticipate ______.
options: advances in agricultural technology that increased food production
the existence of food scarcity in any country
the role of government in the economy
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: advances in agricultural technology that increased food production

Population and Labour Market.text: Preventive checks, in Malthusian theory, refer to measures such as ______.
options: late marriage and moral restraint to reduce birth rates
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: late marriage and moral restraint to reduce birth rates

Population and Labour Market.text: The labour force of a country consists of ______.
options: all persons of working age who are either employed or actively seeking work
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: all persons of working age who are either employed or actively seeking work

Population and Labour Market.text: Human capital refers to ______.
options: the money invested in building factories
the total number of unemployed people in a country
the physical machinery used in production
the skills, knowledge, and health that workers acquire, which increase their productivity
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: the skills, knowledge, and health that workers acquire, which increase their productivity

Population and Labour Market.text: Investment in education and training as a way of improving workers' productivity is best described as investment in ______.
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: human capital

Population and Labour Market.text: Wage, in economics, is best defined as ______.
options: the price paid for the use of land
the reward paid to labour for its services
the return earned by an entrepreneur
the interest paid on borrowed capital
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: the reward paid to labour for its services

Population and Labour Market.text: In a competitive labour market, the wage rate is primarily determined by ______.
options: the personal preference of the worker alone
the age of the employer's company
the interaction of the demand for and supply of labour
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: the interaction of the demand for and supply of labour

Population and Labour Market.text: A wage that is fixed above the market equilibrium wage, such as a minimum wage, may lead to ______.
options: a shortage of workers willing to work
an automatic increase in demand for labour
a fall in the cost of production for firms
an excess supply of labour, causing unemployment
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: an excess supply of labour, causing unemployment

Population and Labour Market.text: Which of the following is a factor that can cause wage differences between two occupations?
options: The level of skill and training required for the job
The number of public holidays in the country
The colour of the workplace building
The distance of the country from the equator
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: The level of skill and training required for the job

Population and Labour Market.text: Unemployment can be defined as a situation where ______.
options: everyone in the country has a job
people of working age who are willing and able to work cannot find jobs
workers are paid very high wages
the population of a country is declining
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: people of working age who are willing and able to work cannot find jobs

Population and Labour Market.text: Underemployment occurs when a worker ______.
options: is working full-time in a job that fully utilizes their skills
has no job at all and is not seeking one
is engaged in work that does not fully use their skills, qualifications, or available time
earns the highest possible wage in the industry
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: is engaged in work that does not fully use their skills, qualifications, or available time

Population and Labour Market.text: Structural unemployment arises mainly as a result of ______.
options: seasonal changes in weather affecting farming
a temporary fall in demand during a recession only
a mismatch between workers' skills and the skills demanded by changing industries
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: a mismatch between workers' skills and the skills demanded by changing industries

Population and Labour Market.text: Frictional unemployment refers to unemployment that occurs when ______.
options: workers are temporarily between jobs while searching for new employment
the economy experiences a prolonged depression
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: workers are temporarily between jobs while searching for new employment

Population and Labour Market.text: Cyclical unemployment is closely associated with ______.
options: fluctuations in the general business cycle of the economy
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: fluctuations in the general business cycle of the economy

Population and Labour Market.text: Seasonal unemployment is most likely to affect workers in which of the following sectors?
options: Agriculture, such as cocoa farming during the off-season
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: Agriculture, such as cocoa farming during the off-season

Population and Labour Market.text: Disguised unemployment describes a situation where ______.
options: workers are openly registered as unemployed with government agencies
an entire factory shuts down permanently
workers refuse to accept any job offered to them
more workers are engaged in an activity than are actually needed, so removing some would not reduce output
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: more workers are engaged in an activity than are actually needed, so removing some would not reduce output

Population and Labour Market.text: A common cause of unemployment in West African countries is ______.
options: rapid population growth outpacing job creation
excess demand for skilled labour over supply
too few school leavers entering the job market
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: rapid population growth outpacing job creation

Population and Labour Market.text: Over-reliance on a single sector, such as oil, without diversifying the economy can contribute to unemployment by ______.
options: creating too many job openings in other sectors
limiting job opportunities to only that sector, leaving other skills underused
guaranteeing full employment for all citizens
eliminating the need for a labour force entirely
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: limiting job opportunities to only that sector, leaving other skills underused

Population and Labour Market.text: A trade union is best defined as an organization of ______.
options: employers formed to fix consumer prices
workers formed to protect and promote the interests of its members
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: workers formed to protect and promote the interests of its members

Population and Labour Market.text: One major function of a trade union is to ______.
options: negotiate for better wages and working conditions on behalf of members
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: negotiate for better wages and working conditions on behalf of members

Population and Labour Market.text: Apart from wage negotiation, trade unions also perform which of the following functions?
options: Providing welfare support and legal assistance to members
Fixing exchange rates for the country
Determining interest rates at the central bank
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: Providing welfare support and legal assistance to members

Population and Labour Market.text: Collective bargaining refers to the process by which ______.
options: individual workers negotiate their wages secretly with employers
trade unions negotiate with employers on behalf of all their members
government fixes all prices in the economy
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: trade unions negotiate with employers on behalf of all their members

Population and Labour Market.text: A strike action by a trade union is best described as ______.
options: a permanent resignation of all workers
a government policy to reduce wages
a temporary and organized withdrawal of labour to press home demands
a method of increasing company profits directly
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: a temporary and organized withdrawal of labour to press home demands

Population and Labour Market.text: One benefit of trade union membership to a worker is ______.
options: a stronger collective voice in negotiating wages and conditions of service
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: a stronger collective voice in negotiating wages and conditions of service

Population and Labour Market.text: A possible disadvantage of trade union activities to an economy is that ______.
options: excessive wage demands can lead to higher production costs and job losses
they eliminate the need for labour laws
they reduce the bargaining power of workers
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: excessive wage demands can lead to higher production costs and job losses

Population and Labour Market.text: The size of a country's population, together with birth rates, death rates, and migration, determines its ______.
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: population growth rate

Population and Labour Market.text: An optimum population is one at which ______.
options: the population is too large for available resources
the birth rate exceeds the death rate indefinitely
output per head or standard of living is at its maximum, given available resources
there are no workers available for employment
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: output per head or standard of living is at its maximum, given available resources

Population and Labour Market.text: A country is said to be overpopulated when ______.
options: its population is smaller than its available resources require
its birth rate equals its death rate exactly
it has more jobs than available workers
its population exceeds what its resources can adequately support at a good standard of living
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: its population exceeds what its resources can adequately support at a good standard of living

Population and Labour Market.text: Which of the following best describes underpopulation?
options: A situation where there are too few people to fully and efficiently exploit a country's available resources
A situation where unemployment is extremely high
A situation where the death rate greatly exceeds the birth rate every year
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: A situation where there are too few people to fully and efficiently exploit a country's available resources

Population and Labour Market.text: Improving human capital through better healthcare and education mainly helps to ______.
options: increase the productivity and efficiency of the labour force
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: increase the productivity and efficiency of the labour force

Population and Labour Market.text: One government policy that can help reduce unemployment is ______.
options: discouraging entrepreneurship and small business growth
promoting industrialization and skills training programmes
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: promoting industrialization and skills training programmes

Population and Labour Market.text: A worker who has a university degree in engineering but is employed as a taxi driver because no engineering job is available is an example of ______.
Population and Labour Market.correct_answer: underemployment

Agriculture.text: Which of the following is classified as a food crop in West Africa?
Agriculture.correct_answer: Yam

Agriculture.text: Which of the following is an example of an export or cash crop grown widely in West Africa?
Agriculture.correct_answer: Cocoa

Agriculture.text: Livestock farming involves the rearing of ______.
options: crops such as maize and rice
animals such as cattle, goats, and poultry for economic use
Agriculture.correct_answer: animals such as cattle, goats, and poultry for economic use

Agriculture.text: Fisheries as a branch of agriculture is mainly concerned with ______.
options: the rearing of cattle for beef
the rearing and catching of fish and other aquatic life
Agriculture.correct_answer: the rearing and catching of fish and other aquatic life

Agriculture.text: Which of the following is a food crop primarily grown for local consumption rather than for export?
Agriculture.correct_answer: Cassava

Agriculture.text: Groundnut, palm produce, and cotton are all examples of ______.
Agriculture.correct_answer: cash or export crops

Agriculture.text: Peasant farming is best described as ______.
options: large-scale mechanized farming run by multinational companies
farming solely owned and operated by the government
small-scale farming carried out mainly with family labour and simple tools
farming carried out only for export purposes
Agriculture.correct_answer: small-scale farming carried out mainly with family labour and simple tools

Agriculture.text: Commercial farming is characterized mainly by ______.
options: farming purely for family subsistence on a tiny plot
farming operated exclusively by cooperative societies
the complete absence of modern farm inputs
large-scale production of crops or livestock mainly for sale and profit
Agriculture.correct_answer: large-scale production of crops or livestock mainly for sale and profit

Agriculture.text: Cooperative farming involves ______.
options: a group of farmers pooling land, labour, and resources together for mutual benefit
a single wealthy individual owning and managing a large farm alone
the government owning and operating all farmland
farming done exclusively by foreign investors
Agriculture.correct_answer: a group of farmers pooling land, labour, and resources together for mutual benefit

Agriculture.text: State farming refers to farms that are ______.
options: owned and managed by private individuals only
owned and managed by the government
Agriculture.correct_answer: owned and managed by the government

Agriculture.text: One major advantage of peasant farming is that it ______.
options: always produces the highest possible output per hectare
guarantees access to modern irrigation systems
requires very little capital and uses readily available family labour
eliminates the need for land entirely
Agriculture.correct_answer: requires very little capital and uses readily available family labour

Agriculture.text: A major disadvantage of peasant farming in West Africa is ______.
options: overproduction leading to falling prices for all crops
excessive government subsidies distorting the market
low output due to reliance on rudimentary tools and small farm sizes
Agriculture.correct_answer: low output due to reliance on rudimentary tools and small farm sizes

Agriculture.text: One advantage of commercial farming over peasant farming is ______.
options: higher output through the use of modern machinery and improved techniques
greater reliance on manual family labour alone
smaller farm sizes leading to lower total output
complete avoidance of any capital investment
Agriculture.correct_answer: higher output through the use of modern machinery and improved techniques

Agriculture.text: Cooperative farming helps small farmers mainly by ______.
options: forcing them to farm individually without support
allowing them to pool resources and access credit and inputs more easily
increasing the cost of farm inputs for each member
preventing them from selling their produce jointly
Agriculture.correct_answer: allowing them to pool resources and access credit and inputs more easily

Agriculture.text: Agricultural marketing refers to the ______.
options: process of growing crops on a farm
activities involved in moving farm produce from the farmer to the final consumer
Agriculture.correct_answer: activities involved in moving farm produce from the farmer to the final consumer

Agriculture.text: A major problem of agricultural marketing in West Africa is ______.
options: excellent all-season roads linking every farm to the market
an oversupply of cold-chain transport for perishables
too few middlemen buying farm produce
poor storage facilities leading to post-harvest losses
Agriculture.correct_answer: poor storage facilities leading to post-harvest losses

Agriculture.text: Price fluctuation of agricultural produce is often caused by ______.
options: the perishable nature and seasonal supply of many farm products
the fact that all crops are harvested at exactly the same time every year without exception
the absence of any buyers in rural areas
Agriculture.correct_answer: the perishable nature and seasonal supply of many farm products

Agriculture.text: One function of agricultural marketing boards, where they exist, is to ______.
options: grow crops on behalf of farmers
provide a guaranteed price and stabilize farmers' incomes
prevent any form of crop export
eliminate the role of farmers in production
Agriculture.correct_answer: provide a guaranteed price and stabilize farmers' incomes

Agriculture.text: An agricultural policy aimed at increasing food production by providing farmers with improved seeds, fertilizers, and credit is an example of ______.
Agriculture.correct_answer: an agricultural input support programme

Agriculture.text: Land tenure reform as an agricultural policy is mainly intended to ______.
options: prevent farmers from owning any land
abolish all forms of land inheritance
improve farmers' access to and security of land ownership
Agriculture.correct_answer: improve farmers' access to and security of land ownership

Agriculture.text: One major problem facing agriculture in West Africa is ______.
options: the widespread use of outdated farming methods and tools
an oversupply of agricultural extension officers
excessive government investment in irrigation everywhere
a surplus of trained agronomists in every village
Agriculture.correct_answer: the widespread use of outdated farming methods and tools

Agriculture.text: Land fragmentation, where farmland is divided into many small, scattered plots, is a problem because it ______.
options: makes mechanized farming and efficient production more difficult
eliminates the need for farm labour
Agriculture.correct_answer: makes mechanized farming and efficient production more difficult

Agriculture.text: Inadequate credit facilities for farmers in West Africa mainly result in ______.
options: farmers being unable to purchase improved inputs and expand production
a decrease in the price of farmland
Agriculture.correct_answer: farmers being unable to purchase improved inputs and expand production

Agriculture.text: Pests and diseases affecting crops and livestock are a major agricultural problem because they ______.
options: increase the overall quality of farm produce
have no effect on farm income
are completely eliminated by traditional farming methods
reduce yields and can wipe out entire harvests or herds
Agriculture.correct_answer: reduce yields and can wipe out entire harvests or herds

Agriculture.text: Rural-urban migration of youths negatively affects agriculture mainly by ______.
options: leaving farming to mostly older people, reducing the active farm labour force
increasing the number of young, able-bodied farm workers
improving the use of modern farm machinery in villages
Agriculture.correct_answer: leaving farming to mostly older people, reducing the active farm labour force

Agriculture.text: Poor road networks in rural farming areas mainly lead to ______.
options: faster movement of produce from farms to markets
difficulty transporting produce to markets, causing losses and higher costs
an increase in farm gate prices received by farmers
Agriculture.correct_answer: difficulty transporting produce to markets, causing losses and higher costs

Agriculture.text: One recommended solution to the problem of low agricultural output in West Africa is ______.
options: discouraging the use of improved seeds and fertilizers
encouraging mechanization and the adoption of modern farming techniques
Agriculture.correct_answer: encouraging mechanization and the adoption of modern farming techniques

Agriculture.text: Providing farmers with easier access to credit through agricultural banks is a solution aimed at addressing ______.
options: the problem of overpopulation in cities
the problem of insufficient capital for farm investment
Agriculture.correct_answer: the problem of insufficient capital for farm investment

Agriculture.text: Improving rural infrastructure such as roads and storage facilities mainly helps to solve the problem of ______.
options: post-harvest losses and difficulty accessing markets
excess rainfall in the Sahel region
Agriculture.correct_answer: post-harvest losses and difficulty accessing markets

Agriculture.text: Agricultural extension services are important because they ______.
options: replace the need for farmers entirely
educate farmers on improved farming techniques and new technologies
eliminate the need for agricultural research
Agriculture.correct_answer: educate farmers on improved farming techniques and new technologies

Agriculture.text: Which of the following best describes mixed farming?
options: The practice of only rearing fish in ponds
The practice of growing a single crop exclusively for export
The practice of growing crops and rearing livestock together on the same farm
The practice of leaving land completely fallow every year
Agriculture.correct_answer: The practice of growing crops and rearing livestock together on the same farm

Agriculture.text: Shifting cultivation is a traditional farming system in which farmers ______.
options: remain permanently on one plot of land using heavy machinery
rear only livestock without growing any crops
move to a new plot of land after the fertility of the previous plot declines
Agriculture.correct_answer: move to a new plot of land after the fertility of the previous plot declines

Agriculture.text: Which of the following is an important export earner classified under livestock or animal products in some West African economies?
Agriculture.correct_answer: Hides and skins

Agriculture.text: One reason government intervenes in agricultural marketing through price stabilization schemes is to ______.
options: increase the risk faced by farmers
protect farmers from sharp fluctuations in world market prices
discourage farmers from producing cash crops
Agriculture.correct_answer: protect farmers from sharp fluctuations in world market prices

Agriculture.text: Subsistence farming differs from commercial farming mainly in that subsistence farming is carried out primarily ______.
options: to meet the food needs of the farmer's own household
Agriculture.correct_answer: to meet the food needs of the farmer's own household

Agriculture.text: Aquaculture, or fish farming, contributes to the agricultural sector by ______.
options: eliminating the need for livestock rearing
reducing the availability of protein sources
providing an additional controlled source of fish for food and income
Agriculture.correct_answer: providing an additional controlled source of fish for food and income

Agriculture.text: A key challenge facing the fisheries sub-sector in West Africa is ______.
options: overfishing and depletion of fish stocks
an oversupply of modern fishing trawlers for every fisherman
excessive government funding for fish farming
too much regulation preventing any fishing activity
Agriculture.correct_answer: overfishing and depletion of fish stocks

Agriculture.text: Government policies promoting agricultural diversification aim mainly to ______.
options: encourage farmers to grow only one type of crop
reduce over-dependence on a single crop or product
restrict farmers to peasant farming methods only
Agriculture.correct_answer: reduce over-dependence on a single crop or product

Agriculture.text: Climate change and irregular rainfall patterns affect agriculture in West Africa mainly by ______.
options: guaranteeing consistently high crop yields every season
eliminating the risk of drought entirely
causing unpredictable planting seasons and reduced crop yields
Agriculture.correct_answer: causing unpredictable planting seasons and reduced crop yields

Agriculture.text: One effective long-term solution to the problem of poor agricultural financing in West Africa is ______.
options: discouraging all forms of farmer cooperatives
removing government support for irrigation projects
restricting farmers from accessing extension services
establishing specialized agricultural development banks offering affordable credit
Agriculture.correct_answer: establishing specialized agricultural development banks offering affordable credit

Industrialization.text: Which of the following is the best definition of an industry?

A place where raw materials are stored

Industrialization.text: In industrial terminology, a plant refers to:

A single production unit or factory belonging to a firm
A single firm operating in various locations
The market for a particular good
Industrialization.correct_answer: A single production unit or factory belonging to a firm

Industrialization.text: A firm in industrial organization is best described as:
options: A single machine used in production
The government agency that licenses industries
A collection of plants under one ownership or management producing goods or services
A group of industries in one country
Industrialization.correct_answer: A collection of plants under one ownership or management producing goods or services

Industrialization.text: Which term describes the totality of firms producing similar goods or services and competing with one another?
Industrialization.correct_answer: Industry

Industrialization.text: Industrial estates are best described as:
options: Areas specially developed with infrastructure for siting industries
Large farms used for cash crop production
Residential areas built only for factory workers
Industrialization.correct_answer: Areas specially developed with infrastructure for siting industries

Industrialization.text: Industries that extract raw materials directly from nature are classified as:
Industrialization.correct_answer: Extractive industries

Industrialization.text: Which of the following is an example of a manufacturing industry?
Industrialization.correct_answer: Textile production

Industrialization.text: Industries that provide intangible outputs such as banking and transport are known as:
Industrialization.correct_answer: Service industries

Industrialization.text: Which of the following industries is classified as a construction industry?
Industrialization.correct_answer: Road and bridge building

Industrialization.text: Agro-based industries obtain their raw materials mainly from:
Industrialization.correct_answer: Agriculture

Industrialization.text: An industry that uses minerals as its major raw material input is called a:
Industrialization.correct_answer: Mineral-based industry

Industrialization.text: Small-scale industries in West Africa are typically characterized by:
options: Large capital investment and heavy machinery
Low capital investment and use of simple tools
Industrialization.correct_answer: Low capital investment and use of simple tools

Industrialization.text: Which of the following best describes a large-scale industry?
options: One with substantial capital, advanced machinery and many employees
One employing few workers with simple tools
One that operates only in rural areas
One that produces only for local consumption
Industrialization.correct_answer: One with substantial capital, advanced machinery and many employees

Industrialization.text: The cottage or craft industry is best described as:
options: Large factories using fully automated machines
Small-scale industry often carried out in homes using simple tools
Industrialization.correct_answer: Small-scale industry often carried out in homes using simple tools

Industrialization.text: Which of the following is a primary industry?
Industrialization.correct_answer: Crop farming

Industrialization.text: A secondary industry is one that mainly:
options: Processes or transforms raw materials into finished goods
Industrialization.correct_answer: Processes or transforms raw materials into finished goods

Industrialization.text: Which factor most influences the location of an industry near sources of raw materials?
options: The need to reduce transportation costs of bulky or perishable materials
The desire to increase government taxes
The need to reduce the number of competitors
The wish to avoid using local labour
Industrialization.correct_answer: The need to reduce transportation costs of bulky or perishable materials

Industrialization.text: Availability of a large market is an important factor of industrial location because it:
options: Reduces the cost of raw materials directly
Ensures a ready outlet for finished goods, reducing distribution costs
Increases the price of raw materials
Has no effect on where an industry is sited
Industrialization.correct_answer: Ensures a ready outlet for finished goods, reducing distribution costs

Industrialization.text: Which of the following is NOT typically a factor influencing industrial location?
options: Availability of power and water supply
Industrialization.correct_answer: Political boundaries of neighbouring countries

Industrialization.text: Industrial localization refers to:
options: The scattering of industries evenly across a country
The relocation of an industry to another continent
The closure of industries due to poor policies
The concentration of a particular industry in a specific area
Industrialization.correct_answer: The concentration of a particular industry in a specific area

Industrialization.text: Which of the following best explains why textile industries in West Africa are often localized near cotton-growing areas?
options: To take advantage of nearness to raw materials
Because government offices are located there
Because labour is generally cheaper in urban areas
Because of favourable climate for machinery alone
Industrialization.correct_answer: To take advantage of nearness to raw materials

Industrialization.text: An important reason industries locate near coastal areas or ports in West Africa is:
options: Lower taxes charged only in coastal towns
Easy access for importing machinery and exporting finished goods
The absence of any competition there
Industrialization.correct_answer: Easy access for importing machinery and exporting finished goods

Industrialization.text: Which of the following is a benefit of industrial estates to small-scale industrialists?
options: They guarantee free raw materials to every firm
They eliminate the need for capital
They provide shared infrastructure like electricity, water and roads at lower cost
They remove the need for skilled labour
Industrialization.correct_answer: They provide shared infrastructure like electricity, water and roads at lower cost

Industrialization.text: Which of the following best describes agglomeration economies as a factor of industrial location?
options: Government subsidies given only to isolated firms
The tendency of industries to avoid urban centres
Taxes imposed specifically on clustered industries
Cost savings that firms enjoy by locating close to other related firms
Industrialization.correct_answer: Cost savings that firms enjoy by locating close to other related firms

Industrialization.text: Government policy such as tax holidays and subsidies is used mainly to:
options: Encourage the establishment and growth of industries
Increase the cost of production for new firms
Reduce the number of industries in a country
Industrialization.correct_answer: Encourage the establishment and growth of industries

Industrialization.text: One major strategy for industrial development in West Africa is:
options: Total reliance on imported finished goods
Banning all forms of foreign investment
Industrialization.correct_answer: Import substitution industrialization

Industrialization.text: Export promotion as an industrialization strategy mainly involves:
options: Producing goods solely for the domestic market
Banning the export of manufactured goods
Encouraging production of goods for sale in foreign markets
Restricting industries to rural areas only
Industrialization.correct_answer: Encouraging production of goods for sale in foreign markets

Industrialization.text: Which of the following is a strategy West African governments use to promote industrialization?
options: Increasing import duties on machinery and raw materials
Restricting access to credit facilities for investors
Provision of infrastructure such as roads, electricity and water
Industrialization.correct_answer: Provision of infrastructure such as roads, electricity and water

Industrialization.text: Establishment of industrial training institutions supports industrialization mainly by:
options: Providing skilled manpower needed by industries
Reducing the number of skilled workers available
Industrialization.correct_answer: Providing skilled manpower needed by industries

Industrialization.text: Regional economic cooperation, such as through ECOWAS, promotes industrialization in West Africa by:
options: Enlarging the market for locally produced goods through trade liberalization
Preventing the free movement of goods
Industrialization.correct_answer: Enlarging the market for locally produced goods through trade liberalization

Industrialization.text: One of the major problems militating against industrial development in West Africa is:
options: Excess skilled manpower in every sector
Inadequate infrastructure such as power and good roads
Industrialization.correct_answer: Inadequate infrastructure such as power and good roads

Industrialization.text: Which of the following best describes import substitution industrialization?
options: Increasing the importation of finished goods
Exporting raw materials without any processing
Producing locally goods that were previously imported
Industrialization.correct_answer: Producing locally goods that were previously imported

Industrialization.text: Export processing zones and free trade zones in West Africa are established mainly to:
options: Attract export-oriented industries with incentives like tax exemption
Restrict industries to import substitution only
Industrialization.correct_answer: Attract export-oriented industries with incentives like tax exemption

Industrialization.text: A key challenge of establishing heavy industries in West Africa is:
options: Excess local capital available for investment
The high cost of machinery and technology
Absence of any raw materials at all
Industrialization.correct_answer: The high cost of machinery and technology

Industrialization.text: Which of the following measures can help reduce the problem of inadequate power supply for industries in West Africa?
options: Investment in additional power generation and alternative energy sources
Increasing dependence on a single overstretched plant
Industrialization.correct_answer: Investment in additional power generation and alternative energy sources

Industrialization.text: The term industrial linkage refers to:
options: The physical distance between two factories
The number of workers employed in an industry
The connection between one industry's output and another industry's input
Industrialization.correct_answer: The connection between one industry's output and another industry's input

Industrialization.text: A backward linkage exists when an industry:
options: Depends on other industries or sectors to supply its raw materials
Sells its output to other industries as raw material
Has no connection with any other industry
Industrialization.correct_answer: Depends on other industries or sectors to supply its raw materials

Industrialization.text: A forward linkage exists when an industry's output:
options: Is used as input by another industry
Is used only for the firm's own consumption
Cannot be sold to any other firm
Industrialization.correct_answer: Is used as input by another industry

Industrialization.text: Government provision of low-interest loans to industrialists is a strategy aimed at:
options: Reducing access to capital for industrial investment
Increasing the cost of borrowing for industries
Easing the financing constraints faced by industrialists
Industrialization.correct_answer: Easing the financing constraints faced by industrialists

Industrialization.text: Which of the following best describes the role of research and development in industrialization?
options: It has no effect on industrial productivity
It is only relevant to agricultural production
It helps improve production techniques and product quality
Industrialization.correct_answer: It helps improve production techniques and product quality

National Income.text: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is best defined as:
options: The total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period
The total income earned by a country's citizens both at home and abroad
The value of only agricultural output produced in a country
The total value of imports minus exports
National Income.correct_answer: The total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period

National Income.text: Gross National Product (GNP) differs from GDP in that GNP includes:
options: Only income generated within the country's borders
Net income earned by citizens from abroad, excluding foreigners' income earned domestically
Only the value of exported goods
The value of government expenditure alone
National Income.correct_answer: Net income earned by citizens from abroad, excluding foreigners' income earned domestically

National Income.text: Net National Product (NNP) is obtained by:
options: Adding net income from abroad to NNP
National Income.correct_answer: Subtracting depreciation (capital consumption) from GNP

National Income.text: Which of the following is the correct formula for NNP?
options: GNP plus Net Income from Abroad
National Income.correct_answer: GNP minus Depreciation

National Income.text: The income method of measuring national income sums up:
options: All factor incomes such as wages, rent, interest and profit earned in an economy
The total value of goods sold in the market
The total government tax revenue collected
The total value of exports only
National Income.correct_answer: All factor incomes such as wages, rent, interest and profit earned in an economy

National Income.text: Which of the following is NOT a factor income included in the income method?
options: Transfer payments such as pensions and unemployment benefits
National Income.correct_answer: Transfer payments such as pensions and unemployment benefits

National Income.text: The output (product) method of computing national income measures:
options: Only the value of imported goods
The total amount of money in circulation
The value of goods and services produced by all sectors of the economy
The wages paid to government workers alone
National Income.correct_answer: The value of goods and services produced by all sectors of the economy

National Income.text: To avoid double counting in the output method, economists use the concept of:
options: Total gross output at every stage
Total imports recorded at each stage
Total wages paid at each stage
Value added at each stage of production
National Income.correct_answer: Value added at each stage of production

National Income.text: The expenditure method calculates national income by summing:
options: Consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports
Only exports minus imports of services
National Income.correct_answer: Consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports

National Income.text: In the expenditure approach, which symbol commonly represents private consumption expenditure?
National Income.correct_answer: C

National Income.text: In the expenditure formula Y = C + I + G + (X - M), M represents:
National Income.correct_answer: Imports

National Income.text: Which method of measuring national income would be most suitable for an economy with reliable records of wages, rents, interest and profits?
National Income.correct_answer: Income method

National Income.text: A major problem in estimating national income in developing countries is:
options: The existence of a large subsistence or non-monetized sector
The existence of too much reliable statistical data
Excessive and overly detailed government record keeping
The overstatement caused by too many economists
National Income.correct_answer: The existence of a large subsistence or non-monetized sector

National Income.text: Double counting in national income accounting occurs when:
options: Only the value of final goods is counted
The value of intermediate goods is counted along with the value of final goods
Depreciation is subtracted more than once by mistake
National Income.correct_answer: The value of intermediate goods is counted along with the value of final goods

National Income.text: Which of the following should be excluded when computing national income to avoid distortion?
options: Transfer payments like gifts and pensions
National Income.correct_answer: Transfer payments like gifts and pensions

National Income.text: National income statistics are useful mainly for:
options: Calculating a single firm's private profit only
Fixing a country's exchange rate directly
Measuring the economic performance and standard of living of a country
National Income.correct_answer: Measuring the economic performance and standard of living of a country

National Income.text: Per capita income is calculated by:
options: Dividing national income by the total population
Dividing national income by the labour force only
Multiplying national income by the population
Dividing government revenue by the population
National Income.correct_answer: Dividing national income by the total population

National Income.text: If a country's national income is 200 billion and its population is 40 million, the per capita income is:
Which of the following statements about a rise in GDP is most accurate?
options: It always indicates an improvement in the wellbeing of every citizen
It always indicates a fall in the country's population
It indicates an increase in total output, though not necessarily improved living standards
It always indicates a decrease in unemployment
National Income.correct_answer: It indicates an increase in total output, though not necessarily improved living standards

National Income.text: National income data can be used by government mainly for:
options: Fixing the prices of luxury goods only
National Income.correct_answer: Economic planning and policy formulation

National Income.text: One major difficulty in measuring national income is:
options: Problems of double counting and incomplete data
Having too much accurate data on the informal sector
Excess cooperation among data collecting agencies
The complete absence of any need for statistics
National Income.correct_answer: Problems of double counting and incomplete data

National Income.text: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP in that real GDP is:
options: Not adjusted for price changes at all
Adjusted for changes in the price level (inflation)
Measured only in a foreign currency
National Income.correct_answer: Adjusted for changes in the price level (inflation)

National Income.text: If nominal GDP is 500 million and the price index is 125 (base year = 100), the real GDP is approximately:
National Income.correct_answer: 400 million

National Income.text: Which of the following best describes depreciation in national income accounting?
options: The increase in value of a country's currency
The rise in prices of consumer goods generally
The growth of a country's population
The reduction in value of capital goods due to wear and tear
National Income.correct_answer: The reduction in value of capital goods due to wear and tear

National Income.text: Which of these is a use of national income statistics?
options: Comparing the standard of living between countries
National Income.correct_answer: Comparing the standard of living between countries

National Income.text: Goods and services NOT usually captured in national income statistics include:
options: Goods sold in the open market
Unpaid household work such as a mother caring for her children
Services rendered by a paid teacher
National Income.correct_answer: Unpaid household work such as a mother caring for her children

National Income.text: A country's GNP is greater than its GDP when:
options: Income earned by foreigners within the country exceeds citizens' income abroad
The country has no foreign trade whatsoever
Income earned by its citizens abroad exceeds income earned by foreigners within the country
Government expenditure is equal to zero
National Income.correct_answer: Income earned by its citizens abroad exceeds income earned by foreigners within the country

National Income.text: Which of the following national income methods relies mainly on data collected from company accounts and productive sectors?
National Income.correct_answer: Output method

National Income.text: The problem of inadequate and unreliable statistical data in national income computation is most severe in:
options: Developing countries with large informal sectors
Highly industrialized countries with strong data systems
Countries with no population at all
National Income.correct_answer: Developing countries with large informal sectors

National Income.text: In national income accounting, net exports refers to:
options: The value of imports minus exports
The value of exports minus the value of imports
The value of goods produced only for the local market
National Income.correct_answer: The value of exports minus the value of imports

National Income.text: Which of the following is an application of national income data at the international level?
options: Comparing the economic performance of different countries
National Income.correct_answer: Comparing the economic performance of different countries

National Income.text: The three approaches to measuring national income (income, output, expenditure) should, in theory, yield:
options: Results that cannot be compared in any way
A value of zero in every case
The same total value of national income
National Income.correct_answer: The same total value of national income

National Income.text: Which of the following best defines Gross National Product at factor cost?
options: GNP valued using the cost of factors of production, excluding indirect taxes and including subsidies
GNP valued at market prices including all indirect taxes
GNP measured only in a foreign currency
National Income.correct_answer: GNP valued using the cost of factors of production, excluding indirect taxes and including subsidies

National Income.text: The difference between GNP at market price and GNP at factor cost is:
National Income.correct_answer: Indirect taxes minus subsidies

National Income.text: National income accounting helps businesses mainly by:
options: Providing information for investment and production decisions
Eliminating the need for market research
National Income.correct_answer: Providing information for investment and production decisions

National Income.text: One limitation of using GDP as a measure of welfare is that it:
options: Always shows an equal distribution of income
Cannot be calculated for any country
Does not account for how income is distributed among the population
National Income.correct_answer: Does not account for how income is distributed among the population

National Income.text: Which of the following would cause an underestimation of a country's true national income?
options: A large informal or underground economy that goes unrecorded
Complete and accurate records of all transactions
The absence of any subsistence production
Full reporting of all business income
National Income.correct_answer: A large informal or underground economy that goes unrecorded

National Income.text: The term circular flow of income illustrates:
options: The flow of goods from one country to another only
The continuous flow of income and expenditure between households and firms
The movement of population between regions
The flow of interest rates over time
National Income.correct_answer: The continuous flow of income and expenditure between households and firms

National Income.text: Which of the following best distinguishes gross from net in national income terms?
options: Gross excludes depreciation while net includes it
Both terms mean exactly the same thing
Gross includes depreciation while net excludes (subtracts) it
Net always refers only to foreign income
National Income.correct_answer: Gross includes depreciation while net excludes (subtracts) it

National Income.text: A rise in a country's national income figures caused solely by inflation rather than real output growth is best described as:
options: A genuine increase in real national income
An increase in nominal national income without a real increase in output
National Income.correct_answer: An increase in nominal national income without a real increase in output

Money and Inflation.text: Before the invention of money, the exchange of goods and services was carried out through:
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Trade by barter

Money and Inflation.text: A major problem associated with the barter system was:
options: The difficulty of finding a double coincidence of wants
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: The difficulty of finding a double coincidence of wants

Money and Inflation.text: Money can be best defined as:
options: Any valuable metal such as gold
Anything generally acceptable as a medium of exchange and in settlement of debts
Only paper notes printed by a central bank
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Anything generally acceptable as a medium of exchange and in settlement of debts

Money and Inflation.text: In the historical development of money, items such as cowrie shells, cattle and salt were used as:
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Commodity money

Money and Inflation.text: The type of money whose value as money is backed only by government decree rather than intrinsic value is called:
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Fiat money

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is an example of representative money?
options: A gold coin used directly in exchange
A paper certificate that can be exchanged for a fixed quantity of gold
A cheque with no bank backing
A cowrie shell used in ancient trade
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A paper certificate that can be exchanged for a fixed quantity of gold

Money and Inflation.text: The primary function of money as a medium of exchange means that money:
options: Is used only to measure a country's population
Cannot be used to settle debts
Is used to buy goods and services, eliminating the need for barter
Serves only as a store of jewellery
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Is used to buy goods and services, eliminating the need for barter

Money and Inflation.text: Money serving as a unit of account means it:
options: Physically stores goods for future use
Cannot be divided into smaller units
Provides a common measure for expressing the value of goods and services
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Provides a common measure for expressing the value of goods and services

Money and Inflation.text: Money functioning as a store of value allows individuals to:
options: Save purchasing power for use at a future time
Immediately lose value once it is earned
Use it only for barter transactions
Avoid the use of banks entirely
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Save purchasing power for use at a future time

Money and Inflation.text: Money acting as a standard for deferred payment means it is used to:
options: Settle debts and future payments such as loans and instalments
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Settle debts and future payments such as loans and instalments

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is a quality of good money?
options: Being difficult to carry from place to place
Being perishable within a few days
Divisibility into smaller units without loss of value
Being unrecognizable and unstable in value
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Divisibility into smaller units without loss of value

Money and Inflation.text: Legal tender refers to money that:
options: Is illegal to use in any transaction
Can be refused by any creditor at will
Must, by law, be accepted in settlement of a debt
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Must, by law, be accepted in settlement of a debt

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following best describes near money or quasi money?
options: Assets like savings deposits and treasury bills that can be quickly converted to cash but are not cash themselves
Coins and notes currently in circulation
Money used only in ancient barter economies
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Assets like savings deposits and treasury bills that can be quickly converted to cash but are not cash themselves

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is an example of near money?
options: A bundle of currency notes in circulation
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A fixed deposit account

Money and Inflation.text: The narrowest definition of money supply (M1) typically includes:
options: Only the gold reserves held by government
Currency in circulation plus demand deposits
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Currency in circulation plus demand deposits

Money and Inflation.text: Inflation is best defined as:
options: A one-time increase in the price of a single good
A general fall in the price level over time
An increase in the value of money
A persistent and general rise in the price level of goods and services over time
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A persistent and general rise in the price level of goods and services over time

Money and Inflation.text: Demand-pull inflation occurs mainly when:
options: Aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply in the economy
Wages and production costs rise independently of demand
The government reduces the money supply
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply in the economy

Money and Inflation.text: Cost-push inflation is primarily caused by:
options: A rise in the cost of production, such as wages or raw materials
An increase in the money supply held by households
A decrease in the cost of imported goods
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A rise in the cost of production, such as wages or raw materials

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following would most likely cause demand-pull inflation?
options: A sudden increase in government spending without a corresponding increase in output
An increase in the supply of goods without any change in demand
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A sudden increase in government spending without a corresponding increase in output

Money and Inflation.text: An increase in the price of imported raw materials leading to higher production costs and prices is an example of:
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Cost-push (imported) inflation

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following describes hyperinflation?
options: An extremely rapid and out-of-control rise in prices
A very slow and mild rise in prices
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: An extremely rapid and out-of-control rise in prices

Money and Inflation.text: One major cause of inflation is:
options: Excessive expansion of the money supply relative to output
An increase in the supply of goods relative to money
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Excessive expansion of the money supply relative to output

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is an effect of inflation on fixed-income earners?
options: An automatic rise in their real income
No effect whatsoever on their welfare
A fall in their real income and purchasing power
A guaranteed increase in the value of their savings
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A fall in their real income and purchasing power

Money and Inflation.text: Inflation tends to benefit which of the following groups?
options: Creditors who are repaid with money that has lost value
Pensioners living on a fixed income
Debtors who repay loans with money that has lost value over time
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Debtors who repay loans with money that has lost value over time

Money and Inflation.text: One effect of persistent inflation on a country's exports is that it can:
options: Make exports more expensive and less competitive in foreign markets
Have no effect on international trade
Guarantee an increase in export volume
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Make exports more expensive and less competitive in foreign markets

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is a monetary measure for controlling inflation?
options: Reducing interest rates to encourage more borrowing
Increasing the interest rate (bank rate) to reduce borrowing and money supply
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Increasing the interest rate (bank rate) to reduce borrowing and money supply

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is a fiscal measure for controlling inflation?
options: Reducing taxation and increasing government expenditure
Reducing government expenditure and increasing taxation
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Reducing government expenditure and increasing taxation

Money and Inflation.text: Open market operations as a tool for controlling inflation involve the central bank:
options: Buying government securities to increase the money supply
Printing more currency to distribute to banks
Selling government securities to reduce the money supply in circulation
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Selling government securities to reduce the money supply in circulation

Money and Inflation.text: An increase in the cash reserve ratio required of commercial banks helps to control inflation by:
options: Reducing the amount of money banks can lend out
Increasing the amount of money banks can lend out
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Reducing the amount of money banks can lend out

Money and Inflation.text: Price control as a measure against inflation involves:
options: Government fixing maximum prices for essential goods
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Government fixing maximum prices for essential goods

Money and Inflation.text: Wage control (incomes policy) helps to reduce inflation mainly by:
options: Guaranteeing continuous wage increases regardless of productivity
Removing all limits on wage negotiations
Limiting excessive wage increases that could push up production costs
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Limiting excessive wage increases that could push up production costs

Money and Inflation.text: Deflation can be defined as:
options: A persistent rise in the general price level
A one-time fall in a single commodity's price
A rise in the money supply only
A persistent and general fall in the price level of goods and services
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A persistent and general fall in the price level of goods and services

Money and Inflation.text: Disinflation refers to:
options: A slowdown in the rate of inflation without prices actually falling
An actual fall in the general price level
A permanent freeze of all prices
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A slowdown in the rate of inflation without prices actually falling

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following best describes stagflation?
options: A situation of falling prices and full employment
A situation of high inflation combined with stagnant economic growth and high unemployment
Rapid economic growth with stable prices
Low inflation with very high employment
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: A situation of high inflation combined with stagnant economic growth and high unemployment

Money and Inflation.text: One social effect of prolonged inflation is:
options: A guaranteed equal distribution of income
Increased hardship for the poor and fixed-income earners
A permanent increase in the value of savings
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Increased hardship for the poor and fixed-income earners

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following best explains why inflation discourages savings?
options: Savings automatically increase in value during inflation
Banks refuse to accept deposits during inflation
Interest rates always exceed inflation rates
The real value (purchasing power) of money saved falls over time
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: The real value (purchasing power) of money saved falls over time

Money and Inflation.text: A central bank's use of moral suasion to control inflation involves:
options: Persuading commercial banks to adopt lending policies that support price stability without using the force of law
Legally forcing all commercial banks to close down
Abolishing the central bank's regulatory powers
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Persuading commercial banks to adopt lending policies that support price stability without using the force of law

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is most likely to result from excessive deficit financing by government?
options: A fall in the general price level
Demand-pull inflation due to increased money supply without a corresponding increase in output
A reduction in the money supply
An increase in the value of the domestic currency
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: Demand-pull inflation due to increased money supply without a corresponding increase in output

Money and Inflation.text: The transition from commodity money to paper (fiat) money mainly occurred because paper money is:
options: Less durable than commodities like cattle
Heavier and harder to transport than gold
More portable, durable and convenient than bulky commodities
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: More portable, durable and convenient than bulky commodities

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following institutions is primarily responsible for controlling the money supply to manage inflation in an economy?
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: The central bank

Financial Institutions.text: Which institution is charged with issuing legal tender currency in an economy?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Central bank

Financial Institutions.text: A key function of commercial banks is to
options: accept deposits and grant loans to customers
issue treasury bills for the government
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: accept deposits and grant loans to customers

Financial Institutions.text: The Bank of Industry in Nigeria was established mainly to
options: accept savings from the general public for daily transactions
provide long-term finance for industrial and manufacturing projects
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: provide long-term finance for industrial and manufacturing projects

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following institutions provides credit specifically for farmers and agricultural projects?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Bank of Agriculture

Financial Institutions.text: Mortgage banks are set up primarily to
options: finance the purchase of company shares
provide loans for building and buying houses
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: provide loans for building and buying houses

Financial Institutions.text: The money market is best described as a market for
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: short-term funds and credit instruments

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is traded on the money market?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Treasury bills

Financial Institutions.text: The capital market deals mainly in
options: long-term securities such as shares and bonds
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: long-term securities such as shares and bonds

Financial Institutions.text: Which of these securities is traded in the capital market?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Debentures

Financial Institutions.text: The Nigerian Stock Exchange is best classified as part of the
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: capital market

Financial Institutions.text: One important function of the central bank is to act as
options: banker and financial adviser to the government
a direct lender of consumer loans to individuals
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: banker and financial adviser to the government

Financial Institutions.text: Credit creation, whereby loans given out generate further deposits, is a distinctive function of
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: commercial banks

Financial Institutions.text: Which body in Nigeria insures the deposits held with licensed banks to protect depositors?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation

Financial Institutions.text: The primary objective of development banks such as the Bank of Industry is to
options: provide long-term capital for development projects that commercial banks may avoid
accept current account deposits from the public
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: provide long-term capital for development projects that commercial banks may avoid

Financial Institutions.text: Microfinance banks mainly serve
options: low-income earners, small businesses and the informal sector
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: low-income earners, small businesses and the informal sector

Financial Institutions.text: A treasury bill is
options: a certificate of ownership in a company
a long-term government bond repayable after 10 years or more
a short-term government security usually maturing within a year
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: a short-term government security usually maturing within a year

Financial Institutions.text: Commercial papers are issued in the money market mainly by
options: reputable companies to raise short-term funds
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: reputable companies to raise short-term funds

Financial Institutions.text: Which institution has the sole responsibility for formulating and implementing monetary policy?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Central bank

Financial Institutions.text: A major function of the capital market is to
options: mobilize long-term savings for productive investment
issue treasury bills on behalf of government
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: mobilize long-term savings for productive investment

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is NOT a typical function of a commercial bank?
options: Providing agency services such as bill payment
Sole issuance of the national legal tender currency
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Sole issuance of the national legal tender currency

Financial Institutions.text: The central bank serves as a "bankers' bank" by
options: selling consumer goods to commercial banks
holding the cash reserves of commercial banks and lending to them in times of need
insuring the deposits of commercial banks
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: holding the cash reserves of commercial banks and lending to them in times of need

Financial Institutions.text: A key distinction between the money market and the capital market is that
options: the money market trades only in shares
the capital market has no regulatory body
the money market operates only outside West Africa
the money market deals in short-term funds while the capital market deals in long-term funds
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: the money market deals in short-term funds while the capital market deals in long-term funds

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is a long-term security traded in the capital market?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Debenture

Financial Institutions.text: In Nigeria, the body that regulates and supervises the capital market is the
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Securities and Exchange Commission

Financial Institutions.text: A major function of insurance companies as financial institutions is to
options: control the level of interest rates in the economy
pool premiums from policyholders and compensate them against losses
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: pool premiums from policyholders and compensate them against losses

Financial Institutions.text: The Bank of Agriculture supports economic activity mainly by
options: providing credit facilities to farmers and agro-based enterprises
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: providing credit facilities to farmers and agro-based enterprises

Financial Institutions.text: The regulation of credit and money supply through interest rates, open market operations and reserve requirements is known as
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: monetary policy

Financial Institutions.text: A share certificate represents
options: a loan owed by a company to a bondholder
part ownership of a company by the holder
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: part ownership of a company by the holder

Financial Institutions.text: A debenture is best described as
options: a certificate showing part ownership of a company
a certificate of long-term debt issued by a company to raise funds
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: a certificate of long-term debt issued by a company to raise funds

Financial Institutions.text: "Lender of last resort" describes a situation where
options: a commercial bank refuses to grant any more loans
the central bank lends to commercial banks when no other source of funds is available
an insurance company pays out a final claim
a development bank closes down its lending operations
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: the central bank lends to commercial banks when no other source of funds is available

Financial Institutions.text: Financial institutions generally support economic activity by
options: consuming the goods and services produced in the economy
fixing the prices of all goods and services
mobilizing savings and channelling them into productive investment
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: mobilizing savings and channelling them into productive investment

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is a development bank rather than a commercial bank?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Bank of Industry

Financial Institutions.text: One importance of mortgage banks to the economy is that they
options: help individuals and firms acquire and develop landed property and housing
regulate activities on the stock exchange
serve as the sole issuer of national currency
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: help individuals and firms acquire and develop landed property and housing

Financial Institutions.text: In the money market, "call money" refers to
options: funds lent for a fixed period of 10 years or more
funds used exclusively to purchase company shares
funds kept permanently as till money
funds lent at very short notice and repayable almost immediately on demand
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: funds lent at very short notice and repayable almost immediately on demand

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is a core function of the central bank?
options: Granting personal loans directly to individual customers
Underwriting insurance policies for the public
Sole issuance of legal tender currency in the country
Trading shares on the stock exchange on behalf of clients
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Sole issuance of legal tender currency in the country

Financial Institutions.text: The stock exchange facilitates the capital market by
options: printing new currency notes for circulation
providing an organized platform where new and existing securities are bought and sold
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: providing an organized platform where new and existing securities are bought and sold

Financial Institutions.text: A key difference between commercial banks and development banks is that
options: commercial banks issue currency while development banks do not
development banks accept public current account deposits while commercial banks do not
commercial banks mainly provide short and medium-term credit, while development banks focus on long-term project finance
there is no real difference between the two types of institutions
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: commercial banks mainly provide short and medium-term credit, while development banks focus on long-term project finance

Financial Institutions.text: A certificate of deposit is best described as
options: a long-term share certificate traded on the stock exchange
a money market instrument representing a fixed-term deposit placed with a bank
a government bond maturing after 20 years
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: a money market instrument representing a fixed-term deposit placed with a bank

Financial Institutions.text: One way commercial banks support economic activity is by
options: providing credit facilities that enable businesses to expand and create employment
directly controlling the nation's exchange rate
issuing treasury bills to the public
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: providing credit facilities that enable businesses to expand and create employment

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following best explains why development banks are important to West African economies?
options: They focus solely on foreign exchange trading
They compete directly with insurance companies for premiums
They mainly provide overnight loans to commercial banks
They provide long-term funds for projects that are often too risky or long-term for ordinary commercial banks
